test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 02 Sept, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A sum of money triples itself at a certain rate of compound interest in 15 years. In how many years will it amount to 81 times of itself?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If a sum becomes **n times** in **t years**, it becomes **nk times** in **t × k years** at compound interest.

Given: Sum becomes **3 times** in **15 years** (n = 3, t = 15).

Target: **81 times** which can be written as **3⁴** (so k = 4).

Required time → 15 × 4 = 60 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 60 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) triples in 15 years ⇒ Amount = **3P**

Time (t₁) = **15 years**

Target Amount = **81P**

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8dbd71ac2ab5d87cdd89b41e83b8a5550bd8d43616cc6fe6e297bc80ceb88f16.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 3P = P(1 + r/100)¹⁵

⇒ 3 = (1 + r/100)¹⁵ ... (i)

We want the sum to become 81 times:

⇒ 81P = P(1 + r/100)t

⇒ 81 = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ 3⁴ = (1 + r/100)t ... (ii)

Substituting the value of 3 from equation (i) into equation (ii):

⇒ [(1 + r/100)¹⁵]⁴ = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ (1 + r/100)⁶⁰ = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ t = 60 years

**∴ The correct answer is 60 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Multiplier

In CI, the amount grows geometrically. If it becomes 'x' times in 't' years, it will become 'x²' times in '2t' years, 'x³' times in '3t' years, and so on.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In **Simple Interest**, the growth is linear. If a sum triples (adds 2P interest) in 15 years, it adds another 2P every 15 years. To become 81 times (add 80P interest), it would take (80/2) × 15 = 600 years.

Rule of 72

A quick way to estimate the time to double an investment: Time ≈ 72 ÷ Interest Rate.</p
